name: Research Reviewer Rejected — Spawn Source-Curator
description: When the research-reviewer terminates with decide(action=insufficient), spawn the source-curator role to evaluate whether the gap is a corpus problem (add sources, wait for indexing, emit curator artifact, decide indexed) OR a research-side issue (decide needs_clarification with retry hint). Replaces the prior researcher-with-source-acquisition retry path under ADR-040 — the curator owns substrate-curation, the researcher stays pure (read curator artifact when present, query, emit). The cognitive-load split was the empirical motivator (smoke #8 run-13 trajectories, ADR-040 §'Why this exists').

on_enter.subject: agent.task.source-curator
on_enter.prompt:
The research-reviewer at loop $entity.instance terminated with decide(action=insufficient). To classify the gap correctly, read TWO sources via read_loop_result: (a) the reviewer's reason on $entity.instance, AND (b) the upstream researcher's open_gaps on $entity.triple.lineage.researcher. The researcher's open_gaps often surface corpus signals ("lack of documentation for X", "queries returned empty for Y") that the reviewer doesn't repeat verbatim — both surfaces inform classification.

If EITHER surface signals a corpus gap (reviewer cites a topic the corpus doesn't cover, OR researcher's open_gaps explicitly cite missing documentation / empty queries): call add_source_repo for each named source, wait for indexing (poll via query_entity until expected entity IDs resolve), then call emit_curator_artifact with the verified entity IDs (and source_dirs if the deployment uses the SemSource shared mount) and terminate with decide(action="indexed", reason="<one-sentence summary of coverage added>"). The next researcher loop will re-attempt the original research with the augmented corpus.

If the reviewer's reason is a research-side issue AND the researcher's open_gaps don't cite corpus shortcomings (the researcher dropped a field, didn't query something obvious, or asked for something the existing corpus already covers): do NOT add sources and do NOT call emit_curator_artifact. Terminate with decide(action="needs_clarification", reason="<why the corpus isn't the issue, citing both surfaces>", retry_hint="<concrete instruction for the next researcher>"). The framework spawns a fresh researcher with your hint via rule 02c.

When ambiguous after reading BOTH surfaces: lean toward corpus gap if the researcher's open_gaps name documentation or query-empty issues; lean toward needs_clarification otherwise. The researcher's signal is just as load-bearing as the reviewer's — researchers know when their queries failed.

metadata.stop_condition: Q2 — MaxIter (=3) + reviewer + opt-in human gate
metadata.max_iterations_note: Aligned to 3 across rules 02/02b/02c for ADR-040 consistency. Each reviewer loop is a new entity so the outer cap is informational under the current rule engine (coordinator.next_action is a single-state terminal); the curator's inner max_iterations=3 is the actionable bound on a single curator pass.
metadata.chain_recovery_cap: ADR-040 §addendum 2026-05-11. The third condition (chain.recovery.proceed eq "true") gates curator spawns at the chain level via cmd/semteams/recoverycounter. The Counter consumes the same agent.complete event the rule does, walks chain ancestry to the chain entity, increments chain.recovery.count, and writes chain.recovery.proceed=true to the triggering reviewer's loop entity ONLY when the new count is within budget (default threshold 3). The KV update from the Counter's write triggers a re-evaluation of this rule on the same reviewer entity; the rule then fires. When the budget is exhausted, the Counter writes chain.recovery.exhausted=true to the chain entity (operator-visible cap-hit marker) and does NOT write proceed — the rule never fires and the chain stalls fail-safe. This split keeps chain-aware logic in the Counter (which has the chain context) and spawn-shape logic in the rule action (which has the persona/tools/prompt template). Counter failure (graph blip mid chain-walk) leaves no proceed → chain stalls without runaway, matching the ADR-040 stance that curator routing is nice-to-have.
metadata.supersedes: configs/rules/research-mode-transition/02-reviewer-rejected-retry-with-source.json (ADR-031 R3.2.2 — researcher-with-source-acquisition path, hard-replaced by ADR-040)
metadata.lineage_forwarding: related_loops.researcher is forwarded from the reviewer's lineage so the curator can read_loop_result on the prior researcher's artifact when classifying. The curator then decides indexed (rule 02b spawns a fresh researcher) or needs_clarification (rule 02c spawns a fresh researcher); both downstream rules drop the lineage.researcher forward per the supersession invariant (the new researcher is the new artifact author).
metadata.operator_toggle: Curator routing is OPTIONAL by design — sources are nice-to-haves, not load-bearing. To disable the curator path entirely (e.g., if curator misclassification is wedging chains in your deployment), set this rule's top-level `enabled` field to false. With curator off, reviewer-rejection ends the chain at the reviewer (no further role spawns from rule 02). Operators who want a non-curator fallback (e.g., re-spawn researcher with extended tools) can author a sibling rule — semteams ships only the curator-on default path. See ADR-040 §addendum 2026-05-11 'Curator optionality' for design rationale + ops workflow.
